propositions: The transition library interface splits the force-bypass concept across force:bool, reason:str, and force_close:str parameters, while claim uses a unified force:str|None parameter carrying the audit reason; transition must adopt claim's canonical shape.

The transition CLI allows --reason to serve as the force-bypass audit note (decoupled from --force), while claim tightly couples the reason to --force=<reason>; the CLI surfaces must unify on --force[=<reason>] as the sole approved pattern.

The internal in-memory name for the force-bypass reason is spelled four different ways (force_reason, force_close, force_close_reason, force_plan_review) across transition and claim; the spelling must be unified to force_reason while retaining the persisted status_data key unchanged.
Legacy callers using transition(force_close='<r>') or transition(force=True) must be mapped to the new force='<r>' parameter via a deprecation alias that warns and preserves behavior.

The guidance text in gates.py, txn.py, and transition.py currently shows multiple incompatible spellings (--force --reason=, --force=<reason>, force_plan_review); all guidance strings must show only --force[=<reason>] and use the unified force_reason internal name.
